description:
The origins of Castello di Tornano probably date to shortly after the year 1000, though some sources cite a first mention as early as 790. In 1167, Emperor Frederick I Barbarossa seized the fief from the Sienese noble Guarnellotto dei Mezzolombardi and granted it to Ranieri de' Firidolfi-Ricasoli, loyal to Florence; however, the rebellious feudal lord, protected by the Sienese, continued occupying the castle for some time afterward. By 1400 the Ricasoli had notably fortified Tornano.

In the 1970s, Castello di Tornano was acquired by the Selvolini family, after having belonged to the Ricasoli barony for centuries. Today it combines accommodation, wine production, and dining in the heart of the Chianti Classico landscape, with panoramic views from its Tuscan-style rooms.

Frederick Barbarossa's 1167 seizure and grant of Tornano to the Ricasoli ties this castle directly to one of the founding moments of a dynasty whose later codification of the Chianti Classico wine formula would shape the entire region's identity for centuries.

The rebellious feudal lord's continued occupation of the castle even after Barbarossa's formal transfer of ownership illustrates the often-contested, slow-moving nature of medieval feudal authority, where a legal grant did not always translate into immediate physical control.

The Ricasoli family's centuries-long stewardship, ending only with the 1970s sale to the Selvolini family, gives Tornano an ownership history spanning roughly eight centuries under a single dynasty before its more recent transition.

The surrounding Chianti Classico wine route and the town of Gaiole in Chianti give guests staying at Tornano direct access to one of Tuscany's most internationally recognized wine-growing regions.
history: Castello di Tornano's origins probably date to shortly after the year 1000. In 1167, Emperor Frederick I Barbarossa granted the fief to the Ricasoli family, who fortified it notably by 1400 and held it for centuries. The Selvolini family acquired the property in the 1970s. Today Tornano combines accommodation, wine production, and dining, with 22 units spread across the main castle building, the medieval tower, and the surrounding borgo.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Castello di Tornano within the main castle building?
faqs.answer: No — the 22 units (Doppel Castle Rooms, Superior Rooms, Tower Suites, and garden apartments) are spread across the main castle building, the medieval tower, and the surrounding small borgo.

faqs.question: What is the connection between Castello di Tornano and the Ricasoli family?
faqs.answer: Emperor Frederick I Barbarossa granted the fief to the Ricasoli in 1167, and the family held and fortified the castle for centuries — the same Ricasoli dynasty later credited with codifying the modern Chianti Classico wine formula.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 10 minutes from Gaiole in Chianti and 40 minutes from Siena by car; Florence's Peretola Airport (FLR) is about 1 hour away.

**Rooms & rates:** 22 units — Doppel Castle Rooms, Superior Rooms, Tower Suites, and garden apartments — spread across the main building, the medieval tower, and the surrounding borgo. From €140/night.

**On-site:** Restaurant serving Tuscan and Chianti cuisine, own winery with tastings, pool in the gardens, tennis court, massages on request.

**Good to know:** Since accommodation is spread across several buildings of the small borgo, confirm at booking whether your unit is in the main castle body or the tower/village annexes.

**Combine with:** Gaiole in Chianti (~10 min), the Chianti Classico wine route, Siena (~40 min), Radda in Chianti.
